questions.question: 46812. A rubber ball is dropped from a height of 2 m. If it rebounds without any loss of velocity, to what height will it rise? (একটি রাবার বল 2 m উচ্চতা থেকে ফেলা হলো। যদি বলটি পুনঃউদ্দীপনে কোনো গতি হারায় না, তাহলে এটি কত উচ্চতায় উঠবে?)
questions.explain:
If a ball rebounds without losing any velocity, it will have the same initial velocity as before hitting the ground. Using the kinematic equation for vertical motion:

v2=u2−2gh, Since the rebound velocity equals the velocity just before impact, the ball will rise to the same height from which it was dropped. Hence, the rebound height = 2 m.

যদি কোনো বল পুনঃউদ্দীপনে কোনো গতি হারায় না, তাহলে এটি প্রাথমিক গতি আগের মতোই পাবে। উল্লম্ব চলনের কাইনেমেটিক সমীকরণ ব্যবহার করলে:

v2=u2−2gh, কারণ পুনঃউদ্দীপনের গতি প্রভাবের ঠিক আগের গতির সমান, তাই বলটি আগের মতোই উচ্চতায় উঠবে। সুতরাং পুনরায় উচ্চতা = 2 m।
[Source: NCTB HSC Physics Book]

questions.question: 46810. Which type of force does not produce any turning effect (rotation) on a body? (নিচের কোন বলের ক্ষেত্রে কোনো ঘূর্ণন প্রভাব সৃষ্টি হয় না?)
questions.explain:
Forces cause rotation when they have a turning effect about a point, i.e., when their lines of action do not meet. Concurrent forces are those whose lines of action pass through the same point. Since they all meet at a single point, they cannot create a turning effect about that point—thus no rotation occurs. On the other hand, non-concurrent and parallel forces can produce torque and cause rotation.
বল তখনই ঘূর্ণন ঘটায় যখন তার কার্যরেখাগুলি কোনো বিন্দুর চারপাশে ঘূর্ণন প্রভাব সৃষ্টি করে। সহাবস্থানী বলের ক্ষেত্রে সব কার্যরেখা একটি বিন্দুর মধ্য দিয়ে যায়। যেহেতু তারা একই বিন্দুতে মিলিত হয়, তাই তাদের কোনো ঘূর্ণন প্রভাব তৈরি হয় না। কিন্তু অসহাবস্থানী বা সমান্তরাল বলের ক্ষেত্রে টর্ক তৈরি হয় এবং ঘূর্ণন ঘটাতে পারে।
[Source: NCTB HSC Physics Book]

questions.question: 46809. If two surfaces are in contact but there is no relative motion or tendency of motion between them, which kind of frictional force comes into play? (যখন দুটি সংস্পর্শে থাকা পৃষ্ঠের মধ্যে আপেক্ষিক গতি বা গতি হওয়ার প্রবণতা থাকে না, তখন কোন ধরনের ঘর্ষণ বল ক্রিয়াশীল হয়?)
questions.explain:
When two surfaces are in contact and there is no relative motion or tendency of motion between them, the force that prevents sliding is called static friction. It acts to oppose the start of motion. Unlike dynamic (kinetic) friction, which acts when surfaces are already moving, static friction ensures stability by balancing applied forces until a threshold limit is crossed.
যখন দুটি পৃষ্ঠ সংস্পর্শে থাকে কিন্তু তাদের মধ্যে কোনো আপেক্ষিক গতি বা গতি হওয়ার প্রবণতা থাকে না, তখন যে বল ক্রিয়াশীল হয় তাকে স্থিতিশীল ঘর্ষণ বলা হয়। এটি মূলত গতি আরম্ভ হওয়া ঠেকিয়ে রাখে। গতিশীল (kinetic) ঘর্ষণের মতো নয়—যেটি চলমান অবস্থায় কাজ করে—স্থিতিশীল ঘর্ষণ প্রয়োগকৃত বলকে সামঞ্জস্য করে বস্তুটিকে স্থির রাখে যতক্ষণ না নির্দিষ্ট সীমা অতিক্রম করা হয়।
[Source: NCTB HSC Physics Book]

questions.question: 46808. The location at which the whole weight of a body may be assumed to act when gravity is distributed over its entire volume is called ______ (যে বিন্দুতে দেহের সমগ্র ওজন ক্রিয়াশীল বলে ধরা হয়, যদিও মাধ্যাকর্ষণ শক্তি আসলে পুরো আয়তনের উপর কাজ করে, তাকে বলা হয় ______)।
questions.option1: Center of gravity of the body (দেহের ভারকেন্দ্র)
questions.option2: The surface of the body (দেহের পৃষ্ঠ)
questions.option4: The centroid of the body (দেহের কেন্দ্রবিন্দু)
questions.explain:
The center of gravity of a body is defined as the point where the entire weight of the body is considered to act, regardless of its actual shape or mass distribution. It represents the average location of the body’s weight under the influence of gravity. While the centroid refers to the geometric center, the center of gravity takes into account the distribution of mass and gravitational force.

কোনো বস্তুর ভারকেন্দ্র হলো সেই বিন্দু যেখানে বস্তুটির মোট ওজন ক্রিয়াশীল বলে ধরা হয়, যদিও মাধ্যাকর্ষণ আসলে বস্তুর প্রত্যেকটি অংশে কাজ করে। এটি মূলত বস্তুটির ভরের বন্টন অনুযায়ী গড় অবস্থান নির্দেশ করে। এখানে লক্ষণীয় যে কেন্দ্রবিন্দু কেবল আকারের উপর নির্ভর করে, কিন্তু ভারকেন্দ্র ভরের বন্টন ও মাধ্যাকর্ষণ বলের উপর নির্ভরশীল।
[Source: NCTB HSC Physics Book]

questions.question: 46807. What does Kinematics deal with? (কাইনেমেটিক্স কিসের সাথে সম্পর্কিত?)
questions.option1: Motion of bodies is studied along with the forces acting on them (বলসহ বস্তুর গতি বিশ্লেষণ করা হয়)
questions.option2: Study of objects that remain stationary (যেসব বস্তু স্থির থাকে তাদের অধ্যয়ন করা হয়)
questions.option3: Motion of bodies is studied without analyzing the cause of motion (বল বা কারণ বিবেচনা না করে শুধু বস্তুর গতি আলোচনা করা হয়)
questions.option4: Study limited only to motion, ignoring other factors (শুধু গতি নিয়েই আলোচনা করা হয়, অন্য কিছু বিবেচনা করা হয় না)
questions.explain:
Kinematics is a branch of mechanics that deals with the description of motion without considering the forces responsible for it. It focuses on parameters such as displacement, velocity, acceleration, and time. Kinematics explains how objects move, but it does not explain why they move. In contrast, dynamics deals with both motion and the forces causing it.

কাইনেমেটিক্স হলো মেকানিক্স-এর একটি শাখা যেখানে বলের কারণ বিবেচনা না করেই শুধু গতি বর্ণনা করা হয়। এখানে displacement, velocity, acceleration, এবং time-এর মতো বিষয়গুলো আলোচনা করা হয়। কাইনেমেটিক্স বলে দেয় কিভাবে বস্তু গতি করছে, কিন্তু নয় কেন গতি করছে। অপরদিকে ডাইনামিক্সে গতি ও তার সাথে সংশ্লিষ্ট বল উভয়ই বিবেচনা করা হয়।
[Source: NCTB HSC Physics Book]

questions.question: 46806. The color tag of Breeder seed is:
46805. Multi-Location Trials (MLT) are conducted to test:
questions.explain:
Multi-Location Trials (MLT) are conducted to test adaptability and performance across regions. 

MLTs are a crucial step in the plant breeding and variety development process. A plant variety that performs well in one location (due to specific soil, climate, and pest conditions) may not perform as well in another.

Multi-Location Trials (MLT) are conducted to evaluate a new crop variety in different agro-climatic regions. The aim is to check:

Adaptability → how well the variety performs under varied environments.
Stability → consistent yield and quality across regions.
Performance → resistance to local stresses like pests, diseases, and climate.

questions.question: 46804. Glyphosate-resistant soybean is an example of:
questions.explain:
Glyphosate-resistant soybean is a genetically modified (GM) crop that can tolerate the herbicide glyphosate (commercially known as Roundup). This allows farmers to spray glyphosate to kill weeds without harming the soybean plants.

Pest resistance: Bt cotton, Bt brinjal
- Herbicide resistance: Glyphosate-resistant soybean
- Improved nutrition: Golden Rice (rich in vitamin A)
- Disease resistance: Papaya resistant to Papaya Ringspot Virus

questions.question: 46803. Which sterilizing agent is commonly used for explant surface sterilization?
questions.explain:
Explant sterilized using:
- Ethanol (70%),
- Sodium hypochlorite / Mercuric chloride,
- Sterile distilled water (final wash).
- All operations done in a Laminar Air Flow (LAF) cabinet.

questions.question: 46802. The special environment created by Ca<sup>2+</sup> treatment and heat shock:
questions.option2: Makes bacterial cell membrane permeable to DNA
questions.explain: - In bacterial transformation, treatment with calcium ions (Ca²⁺) and heat shock is used to make bacterial cells competent, meaning their cell membrane temporarily becomes permeable to foreign DNA, such as a plasmid. This allows the bacteria to take up the DNA and express new genes.

questions.question: 46801. The process of gradually adapting plantlets to external conditions is called:
questions.explain:
Acclimatization (also called hardening) is the process of gradually adapting in vitro-grown plantlets to external environmental conditions such as natural light, temperature, humidity, and soil. This is essential before transferring tissue-cultured plants to the field to ensure survival and normal growth.

Other options
 Tissue culture → the entire in vitro propagation process
Gene transfer → introduction of new genes into a plant
Callus induction → formation of undifferentiated cell mass in culture

questions.question: 46800. Callus formation occurs due to:
questions.explain:
A callus is a mass of undifferentiated plant cells that forms when plant tissues (explants) are cultured on a suitable nutrient medium with the right balance of plant growth regulators (mainly auxins and cytokinins).

Uses:

Mass clonal propagation of plants.
Genetic engineering (e.g., producing transgenic plants).
Secondary metabolite production in biotechnology.

questions.question: 46799. A major risk in tissue culture operations is:
questions.explain: In plant tissue culture, a major risk is microbial contamination. Even a tiny presence of bacteria, fungi, or viruses can ruin the entire culture because the nutrient-rich media provide an ideal environment for microbial growth

questions.question: 46798. One major advantage of plant tissue culture is:
questions.explain:
Plant Tissue Culture - Growing plant cells, tissues, organs in an artificial nutrient medium under sterile conditions.
Plant tissue culture enables the rapid production of many identical plants from a small amount of plant tissue. This is especially useful for plants that are difficult to propagate by seeds or cuttings, ensuring uniformity and faster multiplication.

questions.question: 46797. Seed certification contributes to:
questions.explain:
Seed certification হলো এমন একটি প্রক্রিয়া যেখানে বীজের genetic purity, physical purity, germination, viability ইত্যাদি পরীক্ষা ও নিশ্চিত করা হয়।
এর ফলে কৃষকরা ভালো মানের বীজ পায় → যা ফসলের uniformity (এক রকম বৃদ্ধি ও বৈশিষ্ট্য) এবং productivity (উৎপাদন ক্ষমতা) বাড়ায়।
Objectives of Seed Certification
- Ensure genetic purity of seeds.
- Maintain high germination percentage.
- Control diseases and pests in seeds.
- Increase crop productivity and uniformity.
- Promote high-quality seed production in the seed industry.

questions.question: 46796. One of the most useful methods for identifying a specific gene is-
questions.explain:
Southern blotting হলো DNA বিশ্লেষণের একটি পদ্ধতি, যা একটি নির্দিষ্ট জিন/সিকোয়েন্স শনাক্ত করতে ব্যবহৃত হয়।
আবিষ্কারক: Edwin Southern (1975) → তাই নাম Southern blot।
এতে DNA fragment গুলোকে electrophoresis করে আলাদা করা হয়, তারপর একটি নির্দিষ্ট DNA probe ব্যবহার করে কাঙ্ক্ষিত জিন শনাক্ত করা হয়।

questions.question: 46795. Certified seeds are usually produced from:
questions.explain:
Breeder seed → Foundation seed → Certified seed
Foundation seed হলো breeder seed থেকে উৎপাদিত, এবং এটি Certified seed উৎপাদনের মূল উৎস।
Certified seed হলো এমন বীজ যা কৃষকদের কাছে বিতরণের জন্য গুণগত মান ও বিশুদ্ধতা নিশ্চিত করে উৎপাদন করা হয়।
তাই Certified seeds কখনো farmer-saved বা market seeds থেকে হয় না, বরং সবসময় Foundation seeds থেকে হয়।

questions.question: 46794. BamHI, HindIII, and PstI are examples of:
questions.explain:
Restriction enzyme → cuts DNA at specific points. (EcoRI, HindIII, BamHI, PstI, TaqI, EcoRV, Hpa II, Mob I)
Start codon (AUG) → signals beginning of protein synthesis.
Stop codons (UAA, UAG, UGA) → signal end of protein synthesis.

questions.question: 46793. A bacterium that has successfully acquired a plasmid is called:
questions.explain:
When a bacterium successfully takes up a plasmid (foreign DNA) through the process of transformation, it is called a transformed bacterium.
Transformation is the process by which a bacterium takes up foreign genetic material (like a plasmid) from its surroundings. This is a key step in genetic engineering and molecular cloning.

questions.question: 46792. Plasmids are mainly found in:
questions.explain:
Plasmid is a small, circular, double-stranded DNA molecule found mainly in bacteria Types of Plasmids
- F plasmid → helps in conjugation (gene transfer between bacteria).
- R plasmid → provides resistance to antibiotics. 
-  Col plasmid → produces bacteriocins (toxic proteins that kill other bacteria).
- Ti plasmid (Agrobacterium tumefaciens) → causes tumors in plants, used in plant genetic engineering.

questions.question: 46791. Recombinant DNA is formed by:
questions.explain: Recombinant DNA: DNA that is formed by combining genetic material from two or more different sources using laboratory techniques, to produce new genetic combinations. Example: Human insulin gene inserted into E. coli bacteria.

questions.question: 46790. Which of the following produces genetically identical plants?
questions.explain:
Clonal propagation is the process of producing genetically identical plants (clones) from a single parent plant. 

Genetic Uniformity: All plants produced are exact copies of the parent.
Methods of Clonal propagation:

Vegetative propagation – cuttings, grafting, layering, rhizomes, tubers.
Plant tissue culture – using techniques like organogenesis or somatic embryogenesis.

questions.question: 46789. The main reason meristems remain virus-free is:
questions.explain:
Meristem Culture – Produces virus-free plants.
Meristematic tissues remain virus-free mainly because:

Rapid cell division – viruses cannot keep up with the fast division of meristem cells.
Lack of vascular connections – viruses often move through phloem and xylem, but meristems lack these connections, preventing virus spread.

questions.question: 46788. Cells grown in a liquid medium with continuous shaking are known as:
questions.explain:
Cell suspension culture is a method used in plant tissue culture to grow plant cells, or small clumps of cells, in a liquid nutrient medium. The medium is continuously shaken, usually by an orbital shaker, to ensure several critical things:

Uniform distribution: Shaking keeps the cells from settling at the bottom of the flask, ensuring they are evenly distributed throughout the medium.
Nutrient and oxygen availability: Continuous agitation ensures that every cell has equal access to the nutrients in the medium and that oxygen is properly mixed in, which is crucial for cell respiration and growth

questions.question: 46787. A mass of undifferentiated plant cells grown from explants is called:
questions.explain:
Callus is an unorganized, proliferating mass of undifferentiated plant cells. It is typically induced to grow in a lab setting (in vitro) from a piece of plant tissue, known as an explant, placed on a solid nutrient medium. 
Meristem culture is a specific type of tissue culture that uses meristematic tissue (the actively dividing tips of shoots or roots) as the explant. This technique is often used to produce virus-free plants because the meristematic regions are generally free from viruses.
Suspension culture involves growing single plant cells or small groups of cells in a liquid nutrient medium. The medium is continuously agitated to keep the cells in suspension, allowing for rapid and uniform growth.
Organ culture is a technique for growing an entire plant organ (such as a root, stem, or embryo) in vitro. The goal is to maintain the organ's structure and function, rather than to produce an undifferentiated mass of cells.

questions.question: 46786. Autoclaving in tissue culture is done at:
questions.explain:
Sterilization
- To prevent microbial contamination.
- Autoclave - High temperature (121°C) and pressure (15 psi) maintained for 15–20 minutes kills all microbes and spores.
Explant sterilized using:
- Ethanol (70%),
- Sodium hypochlorite / Mercuric chloride,
- Sterile distilled water (final wash).
- All operations done in a Laminar Air Flow (LAF) cabinet

questions.question: 46785. The most commonly used carbon source in plant tissue culture medium is:
questions.explain:
In plant tissue culture, sucrose is the most commonly used carbon source because:

It is readily metabolized by plant cells.
It provides energy for growth and development.
It acts as an osmotic agent, maintaining proper medium balance.
It acts as Energy Source:, Transport Sugar, Stability:, Osmotic Regulation:

questions.question: 46784. Genome mapping and sequencing helps in:
questions.explain:
Genome Mapping is like creating a high-level street map of a city. It pinpoints the location of genes and other important DNA landmarks on chromosomes and shows the relative distances between them. This is done without reading the exact DNA sequence.

Genome Sequencing is like writing out the exact address of every single house on that street map. It determines the precise order of the four nucleotide bases (A, T, C, and G) that make up a DNA molecule. A complete genome sequence is the ultimate physical map.

(জিনোম ম্যাপিং হলো এমন একটি প্রক্রিয়া যা শহরের একটি উচ্চ-স্তরের রাস্তার মানচিত্র তৈরির মতো। এটি ক্রোমোসোমে জিন এবং অন্যান্য গুরুত্বপূর্ণ DNA ল্যান্ডমার্কের অবস্থান নির্ধারণ করে এবং তাদের আপেক্ষিক দূরত্ব দেখায়। এটি করা হয় সঠিক DNA ক্রম পড়া ছাড়াই।

জিনোম সিকোয়েন্সিং হলো সেই রাস্তার মানচিত্রে প্রতিটি বাড়ির সঠিক ঠিকানা লেখা। এটি নির্ধারণ করে চারটি নিউক্লিওটাইড বেসের (A, T, C, এবং G) সঠিক ক্রম, যা DNA অণুকে তৈরি করে। একটি সম্পূর্ণ জিনোম সিকোয়েন্স হলো চূড়ান্ত শারীরিক মানচিত্র।)

questions.question: 46783. The direct modification of plant DNA using recombinant DNA technology produces:
questions.explain:
Transgenic plants = যেসব উদ্ভিদের DNA তে recombinant DNA technology ব্যবহার করে নতুন জিন (same species বা অন্য species থেকে) প্রবেশ করানো হয়।
এর মাধ্যমে উদ্ভিদের কাঙ্ক্ষিত বৈশিষ্ট্য যেমন → রোগ প্রতিরোধ ক্ষমতা, কীট প্রতিরোধ ক্ষমতা, পুষ্টিগুণ বৃদ্ধি ইত্যাদি অর্জন করা যায়।

Apomictic plants → বীজ তৈরি করে কিন্তু যৌন প্রজনন ছাড়াই (asexual seed formation)।
Hybrid plants → দুটি genetically ভিন্ন parent থেকে cross করে উৎপাদিত।
Wild plants → প্রাকৃতিকভাবে জন্মানো, জেনেটিকালি পরিবর্তিত নয়।

questions.question: 46779. The method used to transfer DNA-coated particles into plant cells is:
questions.explain:
The gene gun (also called biolistic method) is a technique used to deliver DNA-coated microscopic particles (usually gold or tungsten) directly into plant cells. This method is commonly used in plant genetic engineering, especially for plants that are difficult to transform using Agrobacterium.

Gene gun or Agrobacterium-mediated transfer (for monocot and Dicot plants)

questions.question: 46778. Golden rice is genetically engineered to produce:
questions.explain:
Golden Rice is a genetically modified (GM) rice developed to combat vitamin A deficiency in populations that rely heavily on rice as a staple food.
Rich in beta-carotene, a precursor of vitamin A.
Helps prevent night blindness, immune deficiencies, and other health issues caused by vitamin A deficiency.
The rice grains have a yellow-orange color due to beta-carotene, which gives it the name "Golden Rice

questions.question: 46777. The Ti plasmid is found in:
questions.explain: The Ti plasmid (Tumor-inducing plasmid) is found in Agrobacterium tumefaciens, a soil bacterium. It is responsible for transferring a part of its DNA (T-DNA) into plant cells, causing crown gall disease. This natural gene transfer ability is widely used in plant genetic engineering to introduce new genes into plants.

questions.question: 46776. Bt crops are genetically engineered to resist:
questions.explain:
Bt crops get their name from the bacterium Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt), a soil-dwelling microbe that naturally produces crystal proteins, also known as Cry proteins. These proteins are toxic to specific types of insects, particularly the larvae of moths and butterflies (Lepidoptera), beetles (Coleoptera), and flies (Diptera).
When a susceptible insect pest, like the corn borer or cotton bollworm, eats a part of the Bt plant, it ingests the inactive Cry protein.
The alkaline conditions in the insect's gut activate the protein, which then binds to receptors on the gut lining, causing it to rupture. This leads to the insect's death.

questions.question: 46775. The technique used to amplify DNA in vitro is:
questions.explain:
PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) is a technique used to amplify (make millions of copies of) a specific DNA sequence in vitro.
It uses:

DNA template (the sequence to be copied)
Primers (short DNA sequences to start replication)
DNA polymerase (Taq polymerase)
Nucleotides (dNTPs)

questions.question: 46774. Plasmids are commonly used in genetic engineering because:
questions.explain:
Plasmids are commonly used in genetic engineering because they are ideal vectors (carriers of foreign DNA).

Plasmids are commonly used in genetic engineering because:
Small and easy to manipulate → Plasmids are much smaller than chromosomal DNA, making them easier to isolate and modify.
Self-replicating → They contain an origin of replication (Ori), so they can replicate independently inside host cells.
Multiple Cloning Sites (MCS) → Contain recognition sites for restriction enzymes, allowing easy insertion of foreign DNA.
Selectable markers → Usually carry genes for antibiotic resistance, which helps in identifying transformed cells.
Stable inheritance → Once inside a bacterium, plasmids are stably maintained and passed on to daughter cells.
Versatility → Can be engineered to carry large DNA fragments, reporter genes, or expression systems for producing proteins.

questions.question: 46773. Which enzyme is known as molecular scissors?
questions.explain:
- Restriction endonucleases (restriction enzymes) are called molecular scissors because they cut DNA at specific sequences (recognition sites). This property makes them essential tools in genetic engineering and recombinant DNA technology.

Other options-
DNA ligase → joins (ligates) DNA fragments together
DNA polymerase → synthesizes new DNA strands
Reverse transcriptase → converts RNA into complementary DNA (cDNA)

questions.question: 46772. Somaclonal variation arises due to:
questions.explain:
Somaclonal variation refers to genetic variation observed in plants regenerated from tissue culture. It arises due to stress and changes in in vitro culture conditions, such as the type and concentration of growth regulators, culture duration, and physical conditions.
Somaclonal variation বলতে সেই জেনেটিক ও এপিজেনেটিক পরিবর্তনকে বোঝায় যা উদ্ভিদ টিস্যু কালচার থেকে পুনরায় উদ্ভিদ তৈরি করার সময় ঘটে। যদিও টিস্যু কালচারের প্রধান উদ্দেশ্য হলো জেনেটিকভাবে একরকম ক্লোন তৈরি করা, এই প্রক্রিয়ায় উদ্ভিদের কোষগুলোতে বিভিন্ন চাপ সৃষ্টি হয়, যা মিউটেশন এবং DNA-তে অন্যান্য পরিবর্তন ঘটাতে পারে।

46770. The phenomenon where somatic cells develop into embryos is called:
questions.explain:
Somatic embryogenesis is the process in which somatic (non-reproductive) cells develop into embryos that can grow into complete plants. This is widely used in plant tissue culture for clonal propagation and genetic improvement.
 Organogenesis → formation of organs (shoots, roots) from cultured tissues
Differentiation → process where cells become specialized
Clonal propagation → producing genetically identical plants, but not necessarily via embryos

questions.question: 46769. Which sterilizing agent is most commonly used for surface sterilization of explants?
questions.explain:
উদ্ভিদ explant-কে টিস্যু কালচারের জন্য জীবাণুমুক্ত করার সময় surface sterilization করা হয়।
সবচেয়ে সাধারণ এবং নিরাপদ sterilizing agent হলো Sodium hypochlorite (NaOCl)।
এটি বিভিন্ন ধরণের bacteria, fungi ধ্বংস করে।
Ethanol (70%) → সাধারণত quick dip বা short exposure-এ ব্যবহৃত হয়, প্রধান agent নয়।
Mercuric chloride (HgCl₂) → কার্যকর কিন্তু বিষাক্ত, তাই সচরাচর কম ব্যবহার হয়।
Formaldehyde → গ্যাস বা solution হিসেবে ব্যবহার হয়, কম ব্যবহৃত।

questions.question: 46768. In plant tissue culture, auxin and cytokinin ratio controls:
questions.explain:
Auxin : Cytokinin ratio টিস্যু কালচারে কোষের অঙ্গ (shoot/root) গঠনে গুরুত্বপূর্ণ ভূমিকা রাখে।
High Auxin : Low Cytokinin → Root formation
 Low Auxin : High Cytokinin → Shoot formation
 Balanced Auxin & Cytokinin → Callus formation

questions.question: 46767. The ability of a single plant cell to develop into a whole plant is called:
questions.explain:
Totipotency মানে হলো, একটি মাত্র উদ্ভিদ কোষের ক্ষমতা থাকে পুরো একটি গাছ গড়ে তোলার।

Morphogenesis → কোষ থেকে অঙ্গ-প্রত্যঙ্গ বা গঠন তৈরি হওয়ার প্রক্রিয়া।
Differentiation → কোষ বিশেষায়িত হয়ে নির্দিষ্ট কাজ করার উপযোগী হওয়া।
Organogenesis → অঙ্গ (shoot, root) গঠনের প্রক্রিয়া।
